- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., 0.00 or -0.33) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward drag or lagged mean reversion to prevent overextension.
- In high-event periods (e.g., >18 events/30d, net supply negative), model underestimates downside risk — increase downward bias or add volatility penalty to forecast.
- When bullish sentiment is low but price declines sharply, model often fails to recognize bearish momentum — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of prior day’s range.
- In multi-day auction cycles (e.g., CAP3 EU repeated), model tends to overfit recent auction patterns — smooth forecast over 5–7 day window to avoid short-term noise.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misread trend — use sentiment-weighted moving average to anchor forecast to sentiment direction.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion after extreme swings — apply 3–5 day moving average to dampen outliers.
- When supply net is large negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model tends to ignore supply shock — add supply-weighted downward adjustment to forecast.
